scenes.headline: How DFlash 2 picks better drafts from its own shortlist
scenes.sub: Parallel speculative drafting, plus a path selector and a two-tap convolution
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Drizzle! A fast drafter guesses tokens for a big model to check. DFlash 2 makes it choose better from what it already has.

scenes.text: At the first position, the drafter's top pick is right 85.4% of the time; the right token is in its top sixteen 99.5%. So choose, don't predict.
scenes.say: At the first position, the drafter's top pick is right eighty-five percent of the time. But the right token is in its top sixteen ninety-nine point five percent. So: choose better.

steps.label: Top sixteen candidates at every position
steps.say: At every position of the block, keep the top sixteen candidates. The drafter computed them anyway.

steps.label: Independent top picks can stutter
steps.say: Taking each top pick on its own can stutter: two neighbours both choose 'decoding', and verification kills the block there.

steps.label: One coherent path, one candidate per position
steps.say: Instead, a selector scores every adjacent pair and walks one coherent path, one candidate per position.

parts.note: the drafter's own logit for candidate b
parts.say: First, the drafter's own score for candidate b.

parts.note: does b follow a? 256-dim embeddings under a context gate
parts.say: Then, how well b follows a: compact embeddings of both, matched under a context gate.

parts.note: every adjacent pair at once, for 2.0M parameters
parts.say: Every pair is scored at once, for two million parameters and point six percent more latency.

scenes.title: Fixing the end of the block

items.say: Choosing can't fix everything. Even the top sixteen decay, down to eighty-seven point eight percent at the last position.
So a two-tap convolution, before and after each sublayer, lets every position read the one before it, still in parallel.
With three percent more parameters, five layers land on the fifteen-layer curve.

scenes.title: Accepted tokens per pass, Qwen3.5-4B
scenes.note: mean over five benchmarks, for 1.3% more cycle latency
scenes.say: Together: five point nine seven accepted tokens per pass, about one more than DFlash, for one point three percent more latency.

scenes.text: Choosing is cheaper than predicting: the shortlist a model already computed often holds the answer.

recap: Keep the top sixteen, score adjacent pairs
Walk one coherent path through them
A two-tap convolution holds the block's end
scenes.say: To recap: keep the shortlist, score the pairs, walk one path, and let each position see its neighbour.
